name: The Beach Boys
hook: A family surf band whose leader stopped touring to make records, borrowed Phil Spector's method to do it, and pushed the Beatles to answer.

blurb.age13: The Beach Boys formed in Hawthorne, California, in 1961: the brothers Brian, Dennis and Carl Wilson, their cousin Mike Love, and their friend Al Jardine. Their early hits were about surfing and cars, and one of them, 'Surfin' U.S.A.', used the tune of a Chuck Berry song. In 1965 Brian stopped touring to stay in the studio, where he used Phil Spector's session musicians to make 'Pet Sounds' (1966). Paul McCartney said the Beatles took ideas from it for 'Sgt. Pepper'.
blurb.adult: Formed in Hawthorne in 1961 and managed at first by the Wilsons' father, Murry, they signed to Capitol in 1962. 'Surfin' U.S.A.' (1963) set new lyrics to Chuck Berry's 'Sweet Little Sixteen'; it was published by Berry's own publisher, Arc Music, from the start, and Berry's name was added to the credits from 1966. Brian Wilson left the touring band in January 1965 after a panic attack in December 1964, and made 'Pet Sounds' (May 1966) mostly with the Wrecking Crew while the band toured. Wilson has described it as his interpretation of Spector's Wall of Sound, and his own stated trigger was the Beatles' 'Rubber Soul'. 'Good Vibrations' (1966) was the most expensive single recorded up to then; the 'Smile' album that was to follow was shelved in 1967. Credit disputes run through the band's history: Mike Love won a 1994 lawsuit for co-writing credit on many songs, including 'Surfin' U.S.A.'.
